newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna fall drags down Jakarta index.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna fall drags down Jakarta index.

text.p: Jakarta shares closed sharply down on Tuesday on continued foreign selling of heavyweight stocks led by clove cigarette maker Sampoerna, brokers said.
The Jakarta index fell 11.53 points, or 1.97 percent, to close at 574.78 points after touching an intra-day low of 573.12 points in mid-afternoon trade.
Losers led gainers by 73 to 46, with 55 counters unchanged.
"The selling pressure on Sampoerna is likely to continue as the market remains worried about the agenda of its upcoming extraordinary general meeting in November," said a foreign broker.
"It could continue to pressure market sentiment on Wednesday and might lead to some foreign selling of other blue-chips," the broker added.
But another foreign broker said there could be possible bargain-hunting on Sampoerna and other heavyweights as prices had fallen sharply.

Brokers said the combined effect of the falls of heavyweight Telkom overnight in New York and limited foreign selling of toll-road operator Citra Marga and conglomerate Bimantara contributed to the pressure on market sentiment.
Sampoerna fell 11.36 percent to 18,725 rupiah on a turnover of 1.9 million shares after touching a low of 18,650 rupiah in mid-afternoon trade.
Brokers said it was due to poor market reaction to its buying of a stake in car manufacturer Astra International coupled with cautioun over a new short-term loan facility.
"Some investors also took profit in other blue-chips which have registed sharp gains previously," said one local broker.
Conglomerate Bimantara fell 75 rupiah to 2,600 on a volume of 962,500 changing hands.
Local operators were seen buying actively on selected small stocks despite the sell-off by foreign investors, brokers said.
"But mostly on speculative interest, no news could be confirmed," said another local broker.
Battery producer Nipress topped the active list with 12.3 million shares traded, rising 225 rupiah to 1,100 on market talk of a possible stock split.
